The Curriculum

18 Live Sessions.
4 Phases. One Protocol.

A structured 18-week journey from longevity foundations to your personal blueprint, taught live, in small classes of 8 to 15.

Phase 1, Sessions 1 to 3 Foundation
Learning Goals
  • Understand aging as a modifiable trajectory, not an inevitability
  • Distinguish lifespan from healthspan and name the compression-of-morbidity target
  • Articulate a personal reason this course matters
50-Minute Flow
  1. Welcome and group norms
  2. Mini-lecture on healthspan, Medicine 3.0, and aging trajectories
  3. Guided exercise visualizing your 80-year curve
  4. Breakout on the default last decade
  5. Group synthesis and shared course language
  6. Intent‑setting close with Longevity Lens preview
Between-Session Work

Three-day lifestyle awareness log, sleep, movement, meals, energy. Descriptive only, no judgment.

Learning Goals
  • Use the Longevity Lens to evaluate daily choices across four domains
  • Establish a baseline in energy, mobility, mental clarity, and emotional resilience
  • Know three field-ready self-assessments with evidence behind them
50-Minute Flow
  1. Recap from Session 1
  2. Lens demo across the 4-domain frame
  3. Live baseline assessment (cardio fitness estimate, grip strength as a mortality proxy, sit-to-stand, subjective scale)
  4. Pair share on which domain surprised you
  5. Choose one priority domain
Between-Session Work

Record three data points, resting HR (7-day average), grip-strength estimate, sit-to-stand count.

Learning Goals
  • Understand glucose as a signal, not a villain
  • Recognize silent metabolic dysfunction in normal-weight people
  • Know why fasting glucose alone misses most of the picture
50-Minute Flow
  1. Log review
  2. Glucose-as-signal mini-lecture (Snyder, Hall 2018, PREDICT 1)
  3. Three-trace case comparison (healthy vs subclinical vs diabetic)
  4. Breakout on which markers to trust
  5. Group synthesis reframing blood sugar from villain to information
Between-Session Work

One fasted-morning mood and energy log, pre- and post-breakfast, three days.

Phase 2, Sessions 4 to 7 Data & Discovery
Learning Goals
  • Define glucose variability and explain why it predicts risk independently of average glucose
  • Understand metabolic flexibility, fuel switching between carbs and fat
  • Identify what drives spikes and what drives recovery
50-Minute Flow
  1. Recap of glucose-as-signal
  2. Mechanics of variability (SD, time-in-range, MAGE)
  3. Case studies on metabolic flexibility
  4. Breakout to map your suspected drivers
  5. Synthesis previewing the continuous glucose monitor lab
Between-Session Work

Predict your top three glucose triggers before the continuous glucose monitor arrives, food, stress, sleep, or movement.

Learning Goals
  • Apply a continuous glucose monitor and interpret the trace
  • Distinguish meaningful patterns from noise across 14 days
  • Understand what continuous glucose monitor data can, and cannot, tell you
50-Minute Flow
  1. Continuous glucose monitor applied live with the class
  2. App walkthrough and trace anatomy
  3. Review three real participant traces from prior classes
  4. Build your personal protocol for the next 14 days of observation
Between-Session Work

Two weeks of blind observation, wear the continuous glucose monitor, log meals and movement, draw no conclusions yet.

Learning Goals
  • Replace good food / bad food with a personal-response framework
  • Read your continuous glucose monitor data as nutrition feedback rather than verdict
  • Identify your three biggest glucose-driving foods
50-Minute Flow
  1. Continuous glucose monitor data review
  2. Mini-lecture on inputs vs responses
  3. Guided exercise to map your personal response map
  4. Breakout pairs share top triggers and surprises
  5. Synthesis sets up plate architecture
Between-Session Work

Build your personal glucose-response map, three foods that spike you, three that don't, three to test.

Learning Goals
  • Apply the protein-fiber-processing frame to any meal
  • Understand why food order changes the curve
  • Recognize ultra-processed food as a glucose multiplier
50-Minute Flow
  1. Plate architecture mini-lecture (protein floor, fiber lever, processing penalty)
  2. Food-order experiment walkthrough (vegetable
  3. Protein
  4. Carb)
  5. Live build of three plates from your kitchen
  6. Pair coaching to redesign one weekly meal you've already tested on the continuous glucose monitor
Between-Session Work

Run the food-order experiment for three days. Same meal, different order. Capture the continuous glucose monitor trace.

Phase 3, Sessions 8 to 13 Lifestyle Systems
Learning Goals
  • Distinguish time-restricted eating from prolonged fasting
  • Understand the autophagy, insulin sensitivity, and circadian arguments, and their limits
  • Choose a fasting window that fits your life and your data
50-Minute Flow
  1. Evidence review, what TRE actually shows in human RCTs, where rodent autophagy data does and doesn't translate
  2. Case studies on women, athletes, and disordered-eating histories
  3. Design a 4-week trial window matched to your continuous glucose monitor and sleep data
Between-Session Work

Test one meal-timing window for the week. Track continuous glucose monitor, energy, sleep, and adherence.

Learning Goals
  • Understand the microbiome as a metabolic organ
  • Connect fiber, fermentation, and short-chain fatty acids to glucose control
  • Recognize gut-symptom patterns worth investigating
50-Minute Flow
  1. Mini-lecture on the gut-brain-glucose axis (vagal tone, SCFA, postbiotics)
  2. Case studies linking dysbiosis to glucose variability and mood
  3. Self-assessment of fiber diversity (30-plants-per-week)
  4. Breakout on what to add before what to remove
Between-Session Work

Track plant diversity for one week, target 30 distinct plants. Note any symptom or energy correlations.

Learning Goals
  • Use movement to lower postprandial glucose without changing the meal
  • Understand steady cardio, cardio fitness, and strength as the foundation of a long life
  • Build a minimum-effective movement plan you'll actually keep
50-Minute Flow
  1. Centenarian decathlon framing
  2. Movement hierarchy (steady cardio base, cardio fitness ceiling, strength pillar)
  3. Live demo of post-meal walks and how they affect blood sugar
  4. Design a weekly movement floor
  5. Breakout pairs commit to a 2-week trial
Between-Session Work

Test a 10-minute post-meal walk after your highest-glucose meal of the day. Capture the continuous glucose monitor delta.

Learning Goals
  • Read overnight continuous glucose monitor data as a sleep quality signal
  • Apply circadian alignment, light, temperature, timing, as the cheapest longevity lever
  • Identify your two highest-leverage sleep changes
50-Minute Flow
  1. Sleep architecture and the metabolic cost of one bad night
  2. Overnight glucose signatures (dawn phenomenon vs disrupted sleep vs late eating)
  3. Self-assessment across light, temperature, timing, alcohol, caffeine
  4. Commit to a 1-week sleep protocol
Between-Session Work

Run a one-week sleep protocol, fixed wake time, morning light, last meal three hours before bed.

Learning Goals
  • See stress on a continuous glucose monitor trace and distinguish it from food
  • Understand the cortisol-glucose loop and its long-tail metabolic cost
  • Build a regulation toolkit ranked by evidence and convenience
50-Minute Flow
  1. The stress-glucose loop and your body's recovery signal
  2. Case review of non-food spikes
  3. Live practice of three regulation tools (slow exhale, box breath, body reset)
  4. Map your top two stressors and choose your default tool
Between-Session Work

Catch one non-food spike during the week. Use a regulation tool inside ten minutes and log the continuous glucose monitor response.

Learning Goals
  • Understand atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease as the dominant longevity threat
  • Read the cholesterol picture better than your annual physical does
  • Treat cardio fitness as a longevity predictor, not just a fitness number
50-Minute Flow
  1. Four Horsemen framing (heart disease, cancer, brain decline, metabolic disease)
  2. The cholesterol numbers that actually matter, Lp(a) tested once in your life
  3. Prevention timeline that starts decades before the event
  4. Cardio fitness norms by age and sex
  5. Set a personal cardiovascular target
Between-Session Work

Order the right cholesterol panel and Lp(a) on your next blood draw. Estimate your current cardio fitness and write your 12-month target.

Phase 4, Sessions 14 to 18 Integration & Blueprint
Learning Goals
  • Read a longevity-grade lab panel, the markers Medicine 3.0 prioritizes
  • Distinguish 'normal' from 'optimal' ranges and know the difference
  • Build a personal panel and cadence you'll actually run
50-Minute Flow
  1. Longevity panel walkthrough (the cholesterol picture, fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity, inflammation, blood sugar, lipid subfractions, hormones, micronutrients)
  2. Optimal vs reference ranges
  3. Live read-through of a sample panel
  4. Build your panel and cadence
Between-Session Work

Build your personal blood panel. Compare against your last labs. Identify three markers you want to move.

Learning Goals
  • Apply the evidence hierarchy, RCT, mechanism, anecdote, to any supplement claim
  • Identify the foundational supplements with the strongest evidence base
  • Know when wearable data changes a decision and when it's just data
50-Minute Flow
  1. Evidence hierarchy and the foundation set (vitamin D3, omega-3, magnesium, creatine)
  2. Context for longevity therapy candidates
  3. Wearable triage (recovery, sleep, cardio fitness)
  4. Audit your own stack and devices
Between-Session Work

Audit your current supplement stack against the evidence hierarchy. Cut what doesn't earn its place. Pick one to test for four weeks.

Learning Goals
  • Treat social connection as a primary longevity driver, not a soft skill
  • Recognize loneliness as a measurable mortality risk
  • Identify one relationship and one purpose practice to invest in
50-Minute Flow
  1. Harvard Study, Blue Zones, and meta-analyses ranking social connection alongside smoking
  2. Self-assessment of your social architecture (close ties, weak ties, community)
  3. Breakout on purpose, ikigai, and the second-half-of-life question
  4. Commit to one relationship and one purpose practice
Between-Session Work

Initiate one social ritual, weekly call, monthly dinner, weekly walk. Schedule the next four occurrences.

Learning Goals
  • Synthesize the program into a written, personal longevity protocol
  • Translate data and experiments into durable systems
  • Identify the minimum effective dose across nutrition, movement, sleep, stress, and your body's signals
50-Minute Flow
  1. Workshop session, draft your blueprint live across nutrition, movement, sleep, stress, and your body's signals
  2. Pair review checking for honesty, specificity, and minimum effective dose
  3. Closing peer-coaching round on the one habit you'll defend first
Between-Session Work

Finalize your written blueprint. Print it. Share it with one person who will hold you to it.

Learning Goals
  • Translate the blueprint into a 90-day execution plan
  • Identify the relapse risks and the systems that prevent them
  • Leave with a peer accountability structure for the year ahead
50-Minute Flow
  1. Reflection on the 18 weeks, what changed, what didn't, what surprised you
  2. Identity-based change and environment design
  3. Build the continuation plan (one habit to defend, one experiment, one number to retest)
  4. Class closes with peer-accountability commitment
Between-Session Work

Execute the continuation plan. Schedule the class check-in. Re-run your priority blood marker at day 90.

What Makes This Different

Why This Course
Is Different

Live, not recorded.

Every session is live with a certified instructor and your classmates. You ask questions in real time and get real answers. Recordings are there if you miss one.

Your data, your curriculum.

You do not memorize facts about glucose or sleep. You watch them move in your own body. CGM readings and lifestyle logs shape every session.

Small classes, real accountability.

You will know your classmates by name and they will know yours. Peer coaching in the final weeks builds the accountability that keeps the protocol alive.

A written protocol you'll keep.

The course ends with your personal longevity blueprint, tested against your body over 18 weeks. The one deliverable designed to outlast the course.

Questions
worth answering.

For ambitious people who want to optimize their health, energy, and longevity through science-backed nutrition, exercise, recovery, and biomarker tracking. Perfect for high performers, wellness enthusiasts, and anyone ready to take a proactive approach to living longer and feeling better.
No. This course is designed for anyone interested in improving their health, energy, and longevity. You don't need a medical, scientific, or fitness background to participate. We break down complex topics into practical, easy to understand concepts and help you apply them to your own life through simple tracking, actionable exercises, and personalized insights.
Each week, you'll join a 50-minute live session with expert instructors and a community of like-minded people focused on optimizing health, performance, and longevity. Sessions combine science-backed learning, real biomarker and CGM data analysis, and interactive discussions around nutrition, movement, sleep, and recovery. You'll leave with a personalized experiment to apply during the week, turning your own data into actionable insights for long-term health and vitality.
No. This program is educational and focused on helping you better understand the science of longevity, nutrition, movement, recovery, and biomarker tracking. We do not diagnose, treat, or provide clinical care. Our instructors help you interpret research, understand your own health data, and build sustainable lifestyle practices. For medical concerns or clinical decisions, please continue working with your physician.
